subject: English
topic: Active and Passive Voice — Advanced Conversions

questions.stem: Change to passive: 'The police arrested the thief last night.'

options.option_text: The thief was arrested by the police last night. (correct ✓)
The thief is arrested by the police last night. (wrong: 'is arrested' = present passive; original is past simple)
The thief has been arrested by the police last night. (wrong: present perfect passive can't be used with 'last night')
The thief had been arrested by the police last night. (wrong: past perfect passive for a simple past sentence is wrong)

questions.explanation: A is correct. Active Past Simple → Passive: was/were + V3. 'Arrested' → 'was arrested.' Object 'the thief' becomes subject. Agent 'by the police' retained. Time expression 'last night' stays.

questions.stem: Change to active: 'A letter was being written by my mother.'

options.option_text: My mother was writing a letter. (correct: past continuous passive → active past continuous ✓)
My mother is writing a letter. (wrong: 'is writing' = present continuous; original is past)
My mother wrote a letter. (wrong: 'wrote' = past simple; original is past continuous)
My mother had written a letter. (wrong: 'had written' = past perfect; original is past continuous)

questions.explanation: A is correct. Passive Past Continuous (was being + V3) → Active Past Continuous (was/were + V-ing). 'Was being written by my mother' → 'My mother was writing a letter.' The agent 'my mother' becomes subject; the original object 'a letter' becomes object in active.

questions.stem: Change to passive: 'Somebody had stolen my wallet.'

options.option_text: My wallet had been stolen. (correct: when agent is 'somebody/someone/they/people' and unspecified, 'by...' phrase is omitted ✓)
My wallet has been stolen by somebody. (wrong: 'has been' = present perfect; original is past perfect)
My wallet was stolen by somebody. (wrong: 'was stolen' = past simple; original is past perfect 'had stolen')
My wallet was being stolen by somebody. (wrong: 'was being stolen' = past continuous passive; original is past perfect)

questions.explanation: A is correct. Past Perfect Active (had + V3) → Passive: had been + V3. 'Somebody had stolen' → 'My wallet had been stolen.' Agent 'somebody' is unspecified → 'by somebody' is dropped. The passive version naturally omits 'by somebody.'

questions.stem: Change to passive: 'We must complete the assignment before midnight.'

options.option_text: The assignment must be completed before midnight. (correct: modal passive = modal + be + V3 ✓)
The assignment must be completing before midnight. (wrong: 'must be completing' is not standard; should be 'completed')
The assignment should be completed before midnight. (wrong: 'should' changes the modal from 'must'; should keep 'must')
The assignment must have been completed before midnight. (wrong: 'must have been' = past necessity; original is about future/present obligation)

questions.explanation: A is correct. Modal + V1 → Passive: Modal + be + V3. 'Must complete' → 'must be completed.' Agent 'we' (general) is dropped. 'Before midnight' retained. Other modals follow same pattern: can→can be, should→should be, may→may be.

questions.stem: Change to passive: 'They have already repaired the bridge.'

options.option_text: The bridge has already been repaired. (correct: present perfect active → present perfect passive = has/have been + V3; agent 'they' dropped ✓)
The bridge was already repaired. (wrong: 'was repaired' = past simple passive; original is present perfect)
The bridge had already been repaired. (wrong: 'had been repaired' = past perfect passive; original is present perfect)
The bridge is already repaired. (wrong: 'is repaired' = present simple passive; tense doesn't match)

questions.explanation: A is correct. Present Perfect Active (have + V3) → Passive: has/have been + V3. 'They have repaired' → 'The bridge has been repaired.' 'Already' is an adverb that stays in the passive. Agent 'they' (impersonal) is dropped.

questions.stem: Change to passive: 'Do not waste water.'

options.option_text: Water should not be wasted. (close — 'should not be wasted' adds a recommendation; exact passive of imperative is 'Let not water be wasted')
Let water not be wasted. (correct: imperative passive = Let + object + not + be + V3 for negative imperatives ✓)
Water is not to be wasted. (different construction — acceptable but not the standard imperative passive)
Water was not wasted. (wrong: past tense passive doesn't capture the imperative meaning)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Negative imperative passive: Let + object + NOT + be + V3. 'Do not waste water' → 'Let water not be wasted.' Positive imperative: 'Open the window' → 'Let the window be opened.' The 'Let...be + V3' construction is the standard form taught in Indian grammar syllabi.

questions.stem: Change to passive: 'Is he writing a novel?'

options.option_text: Is a novel being written by him? (correct: interrogative present continuous passive ✓)
Is a novel written by him? (wrong: 'is written' = present simple passive; original is present continuous)
A novel is being written by him. (wrong: this is a statement, not a question; original is interrogative)
Was a novel being written by him? (wrong: 'was being' = past continuous; original is present continuous)

questions.explanation: A is correct. Interrogative Present Continuous: Is + subject + V-ing + object? → Passive: Is + object + being + V3 + by + agent? 'Is he writing a novel?' → 'Is a novel being written by him?' Keep the auxiliary 'is' at the front to maintain the question form.

questions.stem: Identify the correct passive form: 'They will announce the results tomorrow.'

options.option_text: The results will be announced tomorrow. (correct: future simple passive = will be + V3 ✓)
The results will have been announced tomorrow. (wrong: 'will have been' = future perfect passive; original is future simple)
The results are announced tomorrow. (wrong: present simple passive; doesn't match future tense)
The results shall be announced tomorrow. (acceptable in formal usage but 'will' is more standard for third person)

questions.explanation: A is correct. Future Simple Active (will + V1) → Passive: will be + V3. 'Will announce' → 'will be announced.' Agent 'they' (general/anonymous) omitted. Time adverb 'tomorrow' retained.

questions.stem: Change to active: 'The song has been sung beautifully by Lata.'

options.option_text: Lata has sung the song beautifully. (correct: agent 'by Lata' → subject; present perfect active = has + V3 ✓)
Lata sang the song beautifully. (wrong: 'sang' = past simple; original is present perfect)
Lata sings the song beautifully. (wrong: 'sings' = present simple; wrong tense)
Lata had sung the song beautifully. (wrong: 'had sung' = past perfect; wrong tense)

questions.explanation: A is correct. Present Perfect Passive (has been + V3) → Active: has + V3 (present perfect active). Agent 'by Lata' → becomes subject 'Lata'. Passive object 'the song' → active object. Adverb 'beautifully' retained in same position.

questions.stem: Choose the sentence that is in passive voice:

options.option_text: The children played in the garden. (active: children = subject performing 'played')
She has been reading the newspaper. (active: she = subject performing 'has been reading' — present perfect continuous active)
The newspaper was read by her. (correct: passive — 'the newspaper' = original object now subject; 'was read' = passive verb; 'by her' = agent ✓)
He will write a letter tomorrow. (active: he = subject performing 'will write')

questions.explanation: C is correct. Passive voice identification: (1) subject is acted upon (not performing), (2) verb = be + V3, (3) agent ('by...') may appear. 'The newspaper WAS READ by her' = passive (newspaper is acted upon; 'was read' = be+V3; 'by her' = agent). All other sentences have active subjects performing actions.
